email.body1:
Les, saw GoodShip closed its $25M Series B and is leaning into enterprise shippers.

Scaling into enterprise that fast usually means more in-market accounts than your team can cover before quota catches up, and that is where deals quietly stall. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for GoodShip off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing those tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Les, quick follow-up for GoodShip.

Post-raise, board expectations on enterprise pipeline tend to jump faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap surfaces late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings GoodShip needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Les, last bit of proof for GoodShip.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how GoodShip's reply rate likely compares to other Series-B startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
